title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
book_title: The Cockpit Dashboard: Six Leading KPIs and the Sudhir Singh Execution Audit
question: Which operational metrics predict Coforge's next four quarters before revenue hits the P&L, and has CEO Sudhir Singh actually delivered on his multi-year promises?

epigraph.quote: Reported revenue is the rearview mirror; executable order book and attrition are the headlights.
epigraph.author: Institutional Operations Maxim

web_blocks.html: Judging an IT services firm on past quarterly sales alone is like driving by the rearview mirror. Enterprise transformation deals take 6 to 18 months to ramp up. As a result, six leading operational KPIs signal Coforge's future sales and margins in advance [3, 5, 19]. In Q2 FY27, most of those gauges look strong. Still, DSO working capital and post-Encora debt leverage need close quarterly tracking [1, 5, 19].

web_blocks.takeaway: Five of six operational KPIs—led by a $2.38B executable order book, $1.04B Q2 FY27 order intake, 16.0% EBIT margin, and 10.4% attrition—score decisively positive, while Total DSO stretching to 110 days (₹2,600 Cr net unbilled) and flat QoQ Encora revenue ($147–148M) remain key watch items.

web_blocks.html: A sound audit also tests whether CEO Sudhir Singh delivers on his promises. From FY22 to FY27, Singh used a clear guidance playbook [22]. He avoided rigid annual sales percentage targets that encourage short-term quarter-gaming [22]. Instead, he anchored investors on two measurable goals [22]. First, he vowed to outgrow peers using the 12-month executable order book. Second, he set clear gross-margin, EBITDA, and EBIT bands [22]. Actual results show a strong record, with one clear miss in FY24–FY25 [1, 3, 22].

web_blocks.takeaway: Sudhir Singh has never missed a top-line growth cycle relative to peers over five years; his sole historical friction point was FY24–FY25 margin compression during Cigniti's onboarding, which reversed sharply in FY26–1H FY27.

web_blocks.html: Looking ahead, Coforge's upside rests on turning its $2.38 billion 12-month order book into organic growth past $3 billion [5, 6]. Doing so without another equity-dilutive deal is the real test [5, 6]. Top-5 client share is down to 18.1%, even as Top-5 accounts grew 20.4% YoY in Q2 FY27 [3, 6, 19]. With 47,365 staff across India, LatAm, and the US/UK, cross-sell room is wide [3, 6, 19]. Coforge already proved this playbook by lifting Cigniti's top two accounts from ~$25M to ~$75M [3, 6, 19]. Management also targets 20%–25% G&A savings at Encora [1, 6, 7]. Over the next year, the key test is paying down the $550 million term loan and cutting debtor days below 80 [1, 6, 7].

web_blocks.title: Why the 12-Month Executable Order Book Is Coforge's Best Leading Indicator
paragraphs: Soft 'total contract value' (TCV) headlines often span five to seven years. By contrast, Coforge reports its signed 12-month executable order book every quarter [2, 3, 5]. That figure tracks next-four-quarter sales very closely. It grew from $1.50B in FY25 to $1.75B in FY26 and $2.38B in Q2 FY27 (+45% YoY), giving high near-term visibility [2, 3, 5].

web_blocks.title: Q2 FY27 Verbatim Management Commentary (Oct 23, 2026)
paragraphs: CEO Sudhir Singh: “The 10.1% sequential growth and 40.1% YoY growth in US dollar terms, a 3.8% sequential organic cc growth, a next twelve month signed order book of $2.38 billion, an order intake of over $1 billion and eight large deals, the most the firm has ever signed in a single quarter, have put us firmly on course to be the industry growth leader for the third year running. We are raising our FY27 EBIT margin guidance from 15.5% to 16%. We expect to further improve our EBIT margin to 17% next year; and will be targeting to be amongst top three scaled IT services firms on margins while maintaining our growth momentum.” [5, 14]

CFO Saurabh Goel: “The margin gains are being driven by technology-led efficiency rather than cuts to growth investment. Revenue rose 53% year over year while sales and marketing rose 52% and G&A only 15.6%. No one was let go, and technology allowed growth without extra hiring.” Goel also noted on cash conversion: “The company remains confident of achieving its full-year target of 100% free-cash-flow-to-profit conversion, with the impact of delayed collections expected to correct as the integration progresses.” [14]

book_paragraphs: If you want to know where Coforge's income statement will be twelve months from now, do not start with macro forecasts—start with the six gauges inside Coforge's operating cockpit.

The first and most reliable gauge is the twelve-month executable order book. Unlike vague multi-year deal announcements that can take seven years to trickle into revenue, this number measures signed contracts scheduled for delivery over the next four quarters. In FY25, it stood at $1.50 billion. By Q4 FY26, it reached $1.75 billion. By Q2 FY27, after absorbing Encora and signing $1.04 billion of fresh quarterly deals—including eight large wins anchored by a $230 million UK public-sector engagement—the executable order book jumped 45% year-on-year to $2.38 billion.

book_subsections.title: Margins, Talent Retention, and the Working-Capital Yellow Flag
paragraphs: The next four gauges confirm that this order surge is not being bought with broken unit economics. Operating EBITDA margin hit 20.6% in Q2 FY27, while EBIT margin reached 16.0%—prompting management to raise full-year FY27 EBIT margin guidance from 15.5% to 16.0%. Employee attrition sits at a calm 10.4% (flat sequentially and down from 11.3% in Q1 FY26), utilization stands at 82.4% across 47,365 total staff, and top-five client concentration has fallen to 18.1% even while those top five accounts grew 20.4% year-on-year. One operational nuance to watch: while legacy Coforge grew 3.8% sequentially in constant currency in Q2 FY27, Encora's standalone revenue was flat QoQ at ~$147–148 million, with management guiding Encora to match Coforge's growth pace starting in Q3 FY27.

The sixth gauge, however, flashes yellow: after FY26 annual debtor days stretched to 88, Q2 FY27 Total DSO (including billed receivables, unbilled revenue, and contract assets) climbed another 8 days sequentially to 110 days (65 billed, 26 unbilled, 19 contract assets) as net unbilled revenue rose from ₹2,100 Cr to ₹2,600 Cr during Encora's US-to-India legal-entity contract migration. That unbilled overhang is our primary operational watch item. High utilization above 82% also leaves less spare bench capacity to absorb sudden ramp-ups without hiring, making steady campus and nearshore recruitment essential.

book_subsections.title: Auditing Sudhir Singh's Five-Year Walk-the-Talk Record
paragraphs: Now let us audit CEO Sudhir Singh's five-year walk-the-talk record from FY22 through 1H FY27. Rather than issuing rigid annual percentage revenue targets, Singh has anchored expectations around executable order-book conversion and explicit margin bands. In FY22, he promised above-industry growth and delivered 38% sales expansion to ₹6,432 Cr while holding a 17% operating margin. In FY23, he targeted the $1 billion revenue milestone and crossed it with ₹8,015 Cr in sales.

In FY24, he stumbled slightly on a 50-basis-point gross margin expansion target early in the year, though 12% top-line growth still beat Tier-1 peers. In FY25, integrating Cigniti temporarily compressed operating margins to 14%, sparking skepticism—yet by FY26, Cigniti's standalone EBITDA margin had been lifted from roughly 11% to 19%, its top two accounts had tripled from $25 million to $75 million combined, and consolidated operating margin rebounded 400 basis points to 18%.

In 1H FY27, Q1 and Q2 EBIT margins both hit 16.0%, beating the initial 15.5% full-year guide. When a management team shows you that level of repeatable operational turnaround, you give it earned credibility—while still holding it strictly accountable for paying down the Encora debt and unwinding the ₹2,600 Cr unbilled revenue balance.

callouts.title: Trust, But Verify Working Capital
callouts.text: Sudhir Singh has earned a strong execution reputation on growth and margin recovery. The next test of leadership quality is whether the post-Encora organization converts that 16% EBIT margin into 100% FY27 FCF-to-PAT conversion while shrinking Total DSO from 110 days.

book_subsections.title: What the Six Leading KPIs Tell Us Before Earnings Print
paragraphs: Quarterly EPS is a rearview mirror; leading operational KPIs are the headlights. Across Coforge's business, six indicators tell you whether the next four quarters will beat or miss expectations: (1) 12-month executable order book ($2.38B in Q2 FY27, up 45% YoY), (2) quarterly order intake ($1.04B in Q2 FY27 across eight large deals), (3) LTM voluntary attrition (10.4%, among the lowest in Indian IT), (4) offshore/overall utilization (82.4%, near optimal efficiency without burnout), (5) EBIT margin progression (guided at 16.0% for FY27, targeting 17.0% by Q4 FY27), and (6) Total Days Sales Outstanding (110 days in Q2 FY27 including unbilled and contract assets, our primary watch metric).

When you audit Sudhir Singh's commentary from FY22 through 1H FY27 against actual results, the walk-the-talk score is remarkably strong: Coforge hit its $1 billion revenue milestone on schedule, delivered the Cigniti margin expansion from ~11% to ~19% EBITDA ahead of plan, and raised FY27 margin guidance even while absorbing Encora. The single operational test ahead is converting that $2.38B backlog into cash collections while bringing Total DSO down from 110 days.

book_subsections.title: AI Disruption vs. AI Tailwind: Auditing Coforge's Quasar & Nuuron Platforms
paragraphs: Every investor in Indian IT today must confront the elephant in the room: does generative and agentic AI cannibalize billable headcount? In Coforge's case, the evidence so far points to net market-share gain rather than deflationary contraction. Through its Quasar AI platform, Cigniti's automated quality-engineering suite, and the November 25, 2026 expansion of its Coforge Nuuron platform into agentic cybersecurity vulnerability remediation, Coforge embeds autonomous AI agents directly into large-deal modernization and enterprise security proposals.

In Q2 FY27, winning eight large deals totaling $1.04 billion in quarterly order intake—while expanding EBIT margins to 16.0% and maintaining 10.4% attrition—demonstrates that clients are consolidating vendors toward mid-tier specialists who deliver AI-accelerated outcomes faster than legacy Tier-1 incumbents.

book_callouts.title: The Runway Beyond $2.6 Billion
book_callouts.text: With a $2.38B 12-month executable order book and 18.1% top-5 client concentration, Coforge has clear visibility toward a $3B+ organic run-rate without needing another dilutive mega-acquisition.
